headline: Nvidia is launching a cheaper version of its small DGX Spark AI computer with half the memory, starting at $4,999.
score_reason: Real product and price news for people who run AI on their own machines, but it is a new memory option rather than a new chip.
importance_line: Hobbyists, small teams and researchers who want to run AI models on their own desk get a cheaper way in, though $4,999 is still a lot of money and the starting price may change with memory costs.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that Nvidia's partners Acer, Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI are due to start selling a 64GB version of the DGX Spark on 23 Oct 2026 at prices starting at $4,999, with the same processor, networking chip and memory speed as the 128GB model. The site says memory prices have climbed so far that 128GB machines cost roughly $7,000 to $9,000 where they can be found, and warns that the $4,999 starting price may not hold.
